subtopics.title: The Nature and Measurement of Unemployment

questions.question: The STRICT definition counts a person as unemployed if they are:
options: Of working age, without work, available to start, and ACTIVELY SEEKING work
Anyone who wants a better job
Everyone of working age not currently at work

questions.question: The unemployment rate is calculated by dividing the unemployed by:
options: The LABOUR FORCE — the employed plus the unemployed
The number of employed people only

questions.question: South African unemployment is described as chiefly STRUCTURAL because:
options: It survives upswings — the business cycle alone cannot explain it
It is caused mainly by resignations

questions.question: The expanded rate sits several percentage points above the strict rate because it adds:
options: Seasonal workers in their working months
DISCOURAGED work-seekers — those who want work but have given up searching

questions.question: The graduate whose post starts in three months is experiencing which type, with which remedy?
options: FRICTIONAL — remedied by better information and faster matching

questions.question: The machinist whose factory closed and whose craft no growing industry wants illustrates:
options: STRUCTURAL unemployment — a mismatch of skills and places, answered by retraining and mobility, not job boards

questions.question: Cyclical unemployment is remedied by:
options: Restored DEMAND — public spending, easier credit, export growth reviving derived demand for labour

questions.question: Technological unemployment shares its remedy with structural unemployment because:
options: In both cases the answer is retraining toward the work that machines create and cannot do

questions.question: The historical-structural layer of causes includes:
options: A capital-intensive economy generating few jobs per rand, a schooling system under-producing technical skills, and spatial design placing labour far from work
The weather and global oil prices

questions.question: Search costs — data, transport, printing — belong in the friction layer of causes because they:
options: Tax the poorest seekers hardest, making the search itself unaffordable

questions.question: For the ECONOMY, unemployment means:
options: A stronger fiscus from lower spending
Output forgone inside the production possibility curve, weaker aggregate demand, a fiscus squeezed from both ends, and future capacity lost as skills decay

questions.question: The self-feeding LOOP is:
options: More grants cause more taxes cause more grants
More hiring causes more orders causes more hiring
No wage means no spending, no spending means no orders, no orders mean no hiring

questions.question: The limit of growth as a jobs strategy is that:
options: The COMPOSITION of growth decides everything — a capital-intensive boom can lift output while hiring almost nobody
Growth only helps skilled workers' wages fall
Growth has no connection to hiring

questions.question: Public employment programmes such as the Expanded Public Works Programme should be judged as:
options: A permanent replacement for the formal labour market
A BRIDGE — immediate income, a first work record and public assets, but temporary, budget-funded and needing an onward connection
A programme with no opportunity cost

questions.question: The UIF is funded by:
options: One percent of earnings from the worker matched by one percent from the employer

questions.question: The crucial gap in the UIF net is that:
options: It reaches ONLY former contributors — the never-employed young person, the largest face in the queue, stands outside it

questions.question: Three thousand applications for forty supermarket posts, while an artisan post is re-advertised three times, shows that the queue is:
options: SPLIT BY SKILL — mass queues for unskilled work beside unfilled skilled posts in the same economy
Evenly spread across all skill levels
Caused by people refusing available work
A sign that adverts are working well

questions.question: The first-job loop trapping young applicants is:
options: Every post wants experience, and experience needs a post
Too many qualifications for the market

questions.question: People who stopped applying after a hundred silences appear:
options: Only in the EXPANDED count — the strict count loses them the day they stop searching

subtopics.title: Five Different Reasons for the Same Empty Hands

questions.question: Lerato, between her June diploma and September internship, needs:
options: Nothing structural — hers is a frictional gap, shortened by faster matching

questions.question: Jabu's eleven years of machine skills that no nearby employer wants make his unemployment:
options: Frictional — a better CV will fix it
STRUCTURAL — only training, trades, transport and time reach it
Seasonal — the plant will reopen in summer

questions.question: Pieter's construction crew, cut when the downturn froze building projects, will most likely be rehired when:
options: Demand returns and cranes go back up — his unemployment is CYCLICAL
The app that replaced him is switched off

questions.question: Sizwe, whose ticket-collecting task went to an app, and Naomi, whose packhouse closes for seven months a year, respectively illustrate:
options: TECHNOLOGICAL unemployment (retrain toward what machines cannot do) and SEASONAL unemployment (build off-season income or training)

questions.question: "Never ask only is the economy growing — ask is it growing in ways that need people" warns that:
options: A mechanised expansion can add billions to output and mere dozens to payrolls, while labour-absorbing sectors hire many hands per rand

questions.question: "A bridge is judged by where it lands" means public employment programmes must:
options: Connect onward — to a skill, a certificate or a next employer — or they relieve symptoms without touching causes

questions.question: The UIF stabilises more than the individual household because:
options: Benefit payments keep spending flowing through local shops in downswings, cushioning the circular flow

questions.question: The honest conclusion of the whole topic is that:
options: One bold policy can clear the queue
Only the net matters; the engine and bridge are optional
No single instrument suffices — an engine growing the labour-hungry way, a bridge that lands somewhere, and a net whose hole must be named, matched always to the diagnosed type
